item.title: China opposes any official engagements between its diplomatic partners and Taiwan authorities: FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes official interactions and engagements of any form between the Taiwan authorities and countries having diplomatic ties with China, and does not allow interference in its internal affairs by any external forces, foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a media report that some Panamanian lawmakers recently set up a so-called "Panama-Taiwan parliamentary exchange group" and U.S. lawmakers attended the launch of the group via video link. According to the report, Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino reiterated that "foreign relations are directed by the Executive," and that parliamentarians' engagements with Taiwan "does not mean that the Executive endorses them." There is but one China in the world and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory, Guo said. "We urge those few politicians to see the real picture. To cross the line on the Taiwan question will lead to serious consequences," he said. The establishment of this so-called "parliamentary exchange group" seriously violates the one-China principle upheld by Panama, the spokesperson said. "We noted the statement of the Panamanian government and hope that Panama will honor its commitment to the one-China principle with real actions to uphold the political foundation of China-Panama relations," Guo said. China urges the United States to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiques, stop sending the wrong message to "Taiwan independence" separatist forces, and stop disrupting and sabotaging China-Panama relations, the spokesperson said.

item.title: 48th Chinese Naval Escort Task Group Will Visit Bangladesh, Myanmar and Malaysia: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept 14 -- "The 48th Chinese PLA Navy Escort Task Group recently completed its missions and set off on its return voyage from the Gulf of Aden. En route back to China, the task group will visit Bangladesh, Myanmar and Malaysia," said Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press briefing on Monday. According to the spokesperson, professional exchanges and open ship days will be held during the visits to further enhance the long-standing friendship and strategic mutual trust between China and the three countries and to facilitate the building of a community with a shared future with neighboring countries.

item.title: Chinese defense minister holds talks with Lao deputy prime minister and defense minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun held talks with visiting Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Khamlieng Outhakaysone in Beijing on Monday. Dong said the Chinese military is ready to work with the Lao military to further strengthen high-level exchanges, enhance the quality and efficiency of practical cooperation in various fields, provide strong support for building an all-weather China-Laos community with a shared future in the new era, and safeguard regional stability. Khamlieng Outhakaysone said the Lao side is willing to strengthen high-level communication and exchanges at various levels between the two militaries, and promote practical cooperation across various fields to achieve more outcomes. This year marks the 65th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Laos. Since Sept. 7, the Chinese and Lao militaries have been conducting a joint military exercise in Vientiane, Laos, codenamed "Peace Train-2026," focusing on humanitarian assistance and medical services. The exercise is scheduled to run through late September, making it the sixth joint exercise of its kind between the two militaries since 2017.

item.title: Fueling Japan's neo-militarism will push region toward dangerous vortex: Chinese spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese defense spokesperson on Monday voiced firm opposition to a joint military exercise by Japan, the United States and Australia, warning that moves promoting Japan's military ambitions will drive the region into a perilous vortex. Jiang Bin, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, made the remarks at a press briefing when responding to a query concerning the "Orient Shield 26" exercise, which is being held in Japan from Sept. 8 to 24. This exercise is packaged as a "shield," but in reality it amounts to the forward deployment of strategic offensive weapons. It not only undermines other countries' legitimate security interests, but also heightens the risk of an arms race and military confrontation, and seriously threatens regional security and stability, Jiang said. Japan, as a defeated country of World War II, is prohibited from obtaining offensive weapons by the Potsdam Proclamation and Japan's pacifist constitution itself. However, in recent years, the country has continuously broken the constraints and its exclusively defense-oriented policy, vigorously developed long-range offensive weapons, and leveraged joint exercises with foreign countries to accelerate its "remilitarization," the spokesperson noted. "Any move that fuels Japan's military ambitions will only push the region into a dangerous vortex and will inevitably bring harm to those involved," Jiang warned. China urges relevant countries to respect other nations' security concerns, correct their wrong practices, and play a positive role in regional peace and stability with concrete actions, Jiang added.

item.title: Xi proposes initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a speech when attending the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) NEW DELHI, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday proposed five initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation in areas of AI, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, smart manufacturing, and talent development. Xi made the proposals when attending the second day of BRICS summit in New Delhi. Xi stressed that "greater BRICS" must make greater impacts, achieve greater development, and lay a solid foundation for practical cooperation. "Greater BRICS" should leverage strengths in being rooted in emerging markets and connected with the Global South, uphold openness and cooperation for mutual benefit and win-win outcomes, keep industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded, and foster integrated markets, Xi said. He also noted that "greater BRICS" should build innovation incubators, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries, and make forward-looking plans for future industries, so that emerging technologies can illuminate the path toward common prosperity. Chinese President Xi Jinping poses for a group photo with other leaders attending the 18th BRICS Summit before the second day of the summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 13, 2026. Xi attended the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit here on Sunday. (Xinhua/Wang Ye)

item.title: Xi, Modi conduct in-depth exchange of views, agree China, India should be partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) NEW DELHI, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi conducted here on Saturday a candid and in-depth exchange of views, and reached important consensus that China and India should be partners. The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Xi said China has always viewed and developed its relations with India from a strategic height and with a long-term perspective. Xi noted that he has met with Modi twice over the past two years, guiding bilateral relations from a new start to a further improvement. Institutional exchanges between the two countries have gradually resumed, the list of areas of cooperation has continued to grow, and bilateral trade has reached a new record high, Xi added. Xi said such hard-won progress should be cherished. Noting that China and India have different national conditions, Xi said they can draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development. Amid a turbulent international landscape, China and India, as the world's two most populous countries and important members of the Global South, shoulder important responsibilities, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to keep in mind the future of humanity and the well-being of peoples, work together to promote high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, and contribute more positive energy to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. Underscoring objective and rational strategic perception in calibrating China-India relations, Xi said China and India are partners for cooperation, not rivals. The two countries provide development opportunities for each other rather than pose threats to each other, he added. That is a strategic judgment based on the development stages of the two countries and the international environment, and serves the common interests of both countries and their peoples, Xi said. Xi called on both sides to help each other succeed through win-win cooperation. The two sides, Xi said, should focus on development as their greatest common denominator, while strengthening friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation. He called on the two sides to expand cooperation in people-to-people exchanges, direct flights and other areas to effectively strengthen the public support for bilateral relations. The two sides should also balance and address each other's economic and trade concerns, and promote a sound and stable development of bilateral economic and trade ties, Xi added. Xi called on China and India to draw on political wisdom of mutual respect and understanding to overcome disruptions, urging both sides to pursue parallel progress in bilateral ties and border issues with the two tracks reinforcing each other, so as to maintain peace and tranquility in border areas. He also urged China and India to promote multilateral cooperation with openness and inclusiveness to benefit the world. Xi said the two countries should support each other as rotating chair of the BRICS, strengthen coordination within such multilateral frameworks as the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the Group of 20, stand together in addressing global challenges, and unequivocally uphold international fairness and justice. Modi said he has held several productive meetings with Xi, guiding India-China relations toward a positive direction, which serves the common interests of the more than 2.8 billion people of both countries. The two major civilizations of India and China have, over thousands of years, learned from each other through exchanges and moved forward hand in hand, he said. India always views India-China relations from a strategic height and a long-term perspective, and is willing to be a partner rather than a rival to China, and to regard each other's development as an opportunity rather than a challenge, he noted. India adheres to an independent foreign policy, and the development of its relations with China is not subject to the influence of any third party, he said. India's policy and position on the issues related to Taiwan and Xizang remain unchanged, and it does not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities in India, he said. India is ready to maintain high-level exchanges with China on the basis of mutual respect and mutual trust, strengthen strategic communication, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and enhance people-to-people exchanges, so as to advance bilateral relations to greater heights, Modi said. The two sides should work together to safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas, he added. India thanked China for its support for India's hosting of the BRICS summit and will fully support China in assuming the BRICS chairmanship next year, he said. Modi said India is ready to closely coordinate and cooperate with China to jointly strengthen cooperation among Global South countries, promote a more multipolar world and global economic growth, and serve as a force for stability and progress in a turbulent world. Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
